decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall begin not later than three years from the date of this decision.
Reason: In order to comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

Condition : 2 - The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and specifications: [FP-47CR-06, FP-47CR-07, FP-47CR-08, FP-47CR-09,Design and Access Statement (dtd 30/12/2024, prepared by Design Endeavour Ltd), Daylight and sunlight Assessment (dtd 30/12/2024, ref UF2412-1/DE-1200), Planting and Maintenance Specification, Fire safety statement  � Received on 28/01/2025; FP-47CR-01, FP-47CR-02 A, FP-47CR-03 A, FP-47CR-04, FP-47CR-05 A, BNG Calculation (dtd 16/01/2025, prepared by MMEnvironental Ltd), BNG metric - Received 10/04/2025; Energy Assessment (Rev D)- Received 02/07/2025; Drainage Strategy (Rev C), Drainage Assessment Form, JDA-572-1-1 (A), JDA-572-2-1 (C)- Received- 18/07/2025 ].
Reason: In order to ensure the development is carried out in accordance with the planning permission.

Condition : 3 - The materials to be used in the construction of the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted shall match those used in the existing building, unless otherwise shown on the approved plans.
Reason: In order to safeguard the appearance of the area.

Condition : 4 - No additional windows or openings shall be formed in the side elevation of the development hereby permitted.
Reason: In order to protect neighbours' privacy.

Condition : 5 - Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development Order) 1995 (or any order revoking or re-enacting that order), no enlargement of the premises or any additional structures/buildings/enclosures within the curtilage of the site shall be carried out, other than as shown in the approved drawings, and no additional floor space shall be formed within the building(s) hereby permitted by means of internal horizontal division (new mezzanine level) without prior written approval of the local planning authority.
Reason:  To protect neighbours' living conditions and the character and appearance of the area and to prevent over-intensive use of the site.

Condition : 6 - All rainwater pipes, gutters, and associated fittings serving the existing and proposed dwellings hereby permitted shall be retained and thereafter maintained within the respective curtilage of each property. At no time shall any such features be positioned so as to discharge onto, overhang, or encroach upon adjoining land.
Reason:
To ensure that drainage arrangements are appropriately contained within the site, to safeguard neighbouring amenity, and to prevent any adverse impacts arising from surface water run-off, in accordance with good planning practice.

Condition : 7 - a)	The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Energy Strategy [Energy Assessment (Rev D)] and shall be retained thereafter for the lifetime of the development.
b)	Prior to first occupation of the new dwelling hereby approved, the relevant evidence (e.g. photographs, installation contracts and As-Built certificates under the Standard Assessment Procedure/National Calculation Method) shall be submitted to the local planning authority and approved in writing to show that the development has been constructed in accordance with the approved Energy Strategy, and any subsequent approved revisions.
c)	Prior to first occupation of the new dwelling hereby approved, where a contribution is found necessary to achieve compliance with zero-carbon requirements of the Development Plan, the developer shall have entered into a binding agreement with the Local Planning Authority to pay any carbon offset contribution at the published rate in-force at the time of submitting details pursuant to Part A of this condition. 
Reason: In order to ensure that the development makes the fullest contribution to minimising carbon dioxide emissions.

Condition : 8 - (A) No development above ground level shall take place until details have been submitted to and approved by the local planning authority which demonstrate that:
(i)	At least three of the key elements of the building envelope (external walls, windows roof, upper floor slabs, internal walls, floor finishes/coverings) are to achieve a rating of A+ to D in the Building Research Establishment (BRE) The Green Guide of specification.
(ii)	At least 50% of timber and timber products are to be sourced from accredited Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) or Programme for the Endorsement of Forestry Certification (PEFC) scheme.
(iii)	No construction or insulation materials are to be used which would release toxins into the internal and external environment, including those that deplete stratospheric ozone.
(B) The development shall not be occupied until evidence (e.g. photographs and copies of installation contracts) has been submitted to the local planning authority to demonstrate that the development has been carried out in accordance with the approved details under Part A of this condition. The development shall be maintained in accordance with the approved details at all times thereafter.
Reason: In the interests of sustainable development.

Condition : 9 - Prior to first occupation of the building(s) hereby approved, the development shall have been constructed to achieve an internal water use of 105 litres/person/day or less.
Reason: In order to protect and conserve water supplies and resources.

Condition : 10 - Prior to commencement of groundworks (excluding site investigations and demolition), the applicant must submit a final detailed drainage design including drawings and supporting calculations to include the full site area to the Lead Local Flood Authority for review and approval, aligned with the approved details. The applicant must consider green infrastructure as part of the proposals, in line with the London Plan drainage hierarchy. A detailed management plan confirming routine maintenance tasks for all drainage components must also be submitted to demonstrate how the drainage system is to be maintained for the lifetime of the development. A maintenance owner should be provided.
Reason: To prevent the risk of flooding to and from the site in accordance with relevant policy requirements including but not limited to London Plan Policy SI 13, its associated Sustainable Design and Construction SPG, the Non-Statutory Technical Standards for Sustainable Drainage Systems and Hounslow Council's Local Plan Policy EQ3.

Condition : 11 - No building hereby permitted shall be occupied until evidence (photographs and installation contracts) is submitted to demonstrate that the sustainable drainage scheme for the site has been completed in accordance with the submitted details. The sustainable drainage scheme shall be managed and maintained thereafter in accordance with the agreed management and maintenance plan for all of the proposed drainage components.
Reason: To comply with the Non-Statutory Technical Standards for Sustainable Drainage Systems, the National Planning Policy Framework (Paragraph 103), the London Plan (Policies SI 12 and SI 13) along with associated guidance to these policies and Hounslow Council's Local Plan Policy EQ3.

Condition : 12 - The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approved landscape details including boundary treatment (dwg ref FP-47CR-06).
The landscaping works shall comply with the requirements specified in BS 3936 (1992) 'Specification of Nursery Stock Part 1 Trees and Shrubs', and in BS 4428 (1989) 'Recommendations for General Landscape Operations', and shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use.

Reason: In order to ensure a satisfactory appearance of the site, surrounding area and to promote biodiversity.

Condition : 13 - Prior to the first occupation of the dwelling hereby approved, secure and covered cycle parking facilities for a minimum of two bicycles shall be provided in accordance with the standards set out in the West London Cycle Parking Guidance. The cycle parking facilities shall be retained thereafter and kept available for cycle parking purposes at all times.
Reason: In order to support sustainable transport objectives.

Informative: 
1.	The applicant is reminded that the provision of cycle storage to the rear of the new house hereby approved and as indicated within the approved submission requires the consent of the owner(s) of the land situated between the application site and Belgrave Road, as the proposed access route crosses land outside the applicant's ownership and beyond the application site. Any access works required to facilitate the cycle store, including the creation or alteration of an access to the public highway at Belgrave Road, may require separate legal agreements and/or consents from the relevant landowner(s) and highway authority. This planning permission does not grant consent for any works on land outside the application site and no such works should be undertaken in reliance upon this permission.

Condition : 14 - Either side of the vehicle access hereby approved, visibility splay areas (the depth measured from the back of the footway and the widths outwards from the edges of the access, with a splay of at least 2.4 metres x 2.4 metres) shall be provided before the access and parking area is brought into use.  These areas shall be kept clear of any obstructions to visibility greater than 600 mm in height, including shrubs, planting, boundary walls, fences, gates, other means of enclosure or other structures or objects at all times.
Reason:  To ensure adequate visibility for drivers entering and leaving the site in the interests of pedestrian and vehicle safety.

Condition : 15 - Before the new dwelling hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use, the Local Planning Authority shall be informed of the agreed naming and numbering of the proposed dwellings so that arrangements can be put in place to ensure that, with the exception of a person eligible for a disabled person's badge issued pursuant to section 21 of the Chronically Sick and Disabled Persons Act 1970 (or similar legislation), no resident of the approved new dwelling shall obtain a resident's parking permit. Any occupiers of the approved new dwelling shall surrender any such permit wrongly issued or held.
Reason: In order to protect the free flow and safety of traffic on nearby highways and to support sustainable transport objectives.

Condition : 16 - Before the dwelling(s) hereby approved are first occupied, the developer shall provide to each dwelling a set of containers required at the time of development for household use for the storage and collection of recyclable materials for the purposes of the Council's kerbside recycling service, to the specification then in use by the local authority's recycling collection service and shall notify the Council's refuse and recycling services when the development is first occupied.  The waste and recyclable materials containers shall be stored in a proprietary refuse bin enclosure designed for the purpose to be supplied by the developer and located adjacent to each dwelling. Each dwelling with a private garden shall also be supplied with a garden waste composting bin of at least 220 litres capacity at the same time.
Reason: In order to protect the quality of the local environment and neighbours' living conditions and to endure appropriate means of refuse storage are provided.
description: Erection of a two storey house compromising of three bedrooms with associated car parking, private amenity space, landscaping, cycle and refuse storage. Following the demolition of the existing part side extension and garage.
subdivision_of_building: part side extension will be demolished including garage.
